title: Astronauts filmed Earth rising above the Moon
title_candidates: What a solar eclipse looks like from the Moon
NASA astronauts filmed a solar eclipse from lunar orbit
What the Artemis II crew saw on the far side of the Moon
The view from inside a spacecraft on the far side of the Moon
When four astronauts said we just went sci-fi, this is why
caption:
NASA's Artemis II crew filmed a solar eclipse from lunar orbit. No human had ever captured this angle before.

On flight day seven, the four astronauts swung past the lunar far side, the half of the Moon that always faces away from Earth. As they came back around, Earth passed behind the Moon from their point of view. One of them said it out loud: "We just went sci-fi." The footage of the lunar far side and the eclipse together is something even mission veterans said they had never seen.

This was the first crewed mission near the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. Fifty years later, humans were close enough to film what an eclipse looks like when you are the one in space.
